summary: This change adds a new ESM-only `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` subpath for Deno and edge runtimes, a Deno CI smoke test and a Supabase example. Most of the release risk is in what ships with it rather than in the new subpath. The main Node entry of @cipherstash/stack moves from protect-ffi 0.23.0 to 0.24.0. The previous protect-ffi bump (0.23) brought breaking payload changes and was paired with an EQL bump. This one comes with no changeset, no EQL lockstep change and no upstream changelog in the evidence. The package version is hand-edited to 0.18.0 while a minor changeset is still pending, so the release tooling may publish 0.19.0. That would leave the new example's `^0.18.0` import with nothing to resolve to. The new WASM client keeps the same names as the Node client (`Encryption`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`) but follows a different contract: it throws instead of returning a Result, and it has no null short-circuit. The CLI and wizard move to auth 0.38.0, which ships its native bindings differently. No CI results were available, so every test is exists_not_run.

behaviour_changes.description: The main Node entry of @cipherstash/stack (encrypt, decrypt, query, bulk) now runs on @cipherstash/protect-ffi 0.24.0 instead of 0.23.0. What changed upstream is unknown. packages/protect stays on 0.23.0.

New published subpath export `./wasm-inline` (ESM import condition only, no require branch). Its exports are `Encryption`, `WasmEncryptionClient`, `isEncrypted` and the schema builders. encrypt/decrypt return raw values or throw, with no Result object, no lock context, no bulk or query operations and no null short-circuit.

tsup is now two parallel configs writing to one dist/ with clean:false; a new prebuild script deletes dist. zod and @byteslice/result are now bundled into every main entry (ESM and CJS) instead of being imported at runtime.
packages/stack/package.json version is changed by hand from 0.17.0 to 0.18.0 and no changeset is added. A pending minor changeset for @cipherstash/stack already exists.

@cipherstash/auth moves from 0.36.0 to 0.38.0 for the CLI and wizard, which import its default export for login and credential resolution. It also becomes a new runtime dependency of @cipherstash/stack. auth 0.38 declares per-platform native bindings as optional peer dependencies, so the CLI and wizard now list six platform packages as optionalDependencies.

The stack tsconfig adds customConditions ['node'] because protect-ffi 0.24 uses conditional exports: `node` resolves to the NAPI bindings and `default` resolves to WASM, with a different newClient signature. The stack's public types re-export protect-ffi types such as `Encrypted`.
New CI job wasm-e2e-tests runs a Deno round-trip with the CS_* secrets and fails if they are missing. New vitest unit tests cover normalizeCastAs. New example examples/supabase-worker.

failure_scenarios.title: protect-ffi 0.24 bump in the main Node entry ships without EQL lockstep or payload-compatibility evidence
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer upgrades @cipherstash/stack to the release built from this change and keeps EQL eql-2.3.1 installed, or reads data written by 0.17.x.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: packages/stack/package.json:217 moves protect-ffi from 0.23.0 to 0.24.0 for all main-entry operations. The repo pins EQL in two places, each with a comment saying it must move in lockstep with protect-ffi (tests.yml:21-22, cli installer/index.ts:5-7). Neither changed. The previous bump (0.23) changed payload shape and SteVec encoding defaults and came with an EQL bump (CHANGELOG.md:7-17). Upstream 0.24 release notes were not available. This change was framed as a WASM feature, and it adds no changeset that would describe the bump.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If 0.24 changes payload or search-term encoding, newly written payloads or query terms may not match what the installed eql_v2 functions or older data expect. Encrypted searches can then silently return no or wrong rows, or reads of existing data can fail. The bump would also reach customers with no CHANGELOG entry.

failure_scenarios.title: Hand-set 0.18.0 plus a pending minor changeset publishes an unexpected version and drops the CHANGELOG entry
failure_scenarios.trigger: changesets/action runs `changeset version` on main after this merges.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: package.json:3 is set to 0.18.0 by hand. .changeset/restore-null-guards-in-encryption-ops.md still declares a minor bump for @cipherstash/stack, and CHANGELOG.md's latest entry is 0.17.0. Changesets bumps from the current version, which gives 0.19.0. No changeset is added for wasm-inline or the dependency bumps, although AGENTS.md:179-198 requires one. The Supabase example imports `npm:@cipherstash/stack@^0.18.0/wasm-inline`, and for a 0.x version that caret allows only 0.18.x.
failure_scenarios.consequence: 0.18.0 is never published and the release comes out as 0.19.0. The example and README instructions then fail to resolve the package, and neither the new subpath nor the protect-ffi and auth bumps appear in the CHANGELOG. Publishing cannot be undone, so fixing this needs a further release.

failure_scenarios.title: WASM client reuses the Node API names with a different contract: it throws instead of returning a Result, and encrypts null
failure_scenarios.trigger: A developer ports Node code to the WASM entry, or a plain JS or Deno caller (no type check) passes null or reads `.data` and `.failure`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: wasm-inline.ts:205-224: encrypt/decrypt return the raw protect-ffi value or throw. AGENTS.md:126 says the `{ data } | { failure }` result shape is a contract of the Node entry. WasmPlaintext explicitly accepts null (wasm-inline.ts:108-114) and encrypt has no null guard. The Node EncryptOperation returns null for a null plaintext (encrypt.ts:63-70), and the pending changeset describes null otherwise being encrypted into a real ciphertext.
failure_scenarios.consequence: For an untyped caller, `const { data } = await client.encrypt(v)` yields undefined, which can be written to the database as NULL instead of a ciphertext, a silent data loss. A nullable field is stored as an encrypted null rather than SQL NULL, so IS NULL semantics differ between rows written from the edge and rows written from Node.

failure_scenarios.title: Consumers using moduleResolution 'bundler' get protect-ffi's WASM typings behind stack's public types
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer project type-checks with moduleResolution bundler (for example the Next.js default) without a `node` custom condition, and upgrades stack.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Stack's own tsconfig needed customConditions ['node'] to avoid resolving protect-ffi 0.24's WASM types (tsconfig.json:18-24). The published types re-export protect-ffi types (types.ts:7-13, 29, 38), and the d.ts files keep those imports external. A consumer resolver without the `node` condition will resolve them to the WASM declarations.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Type errors or silently different `Encrypted`/`Client` types in customer builds after a minor upgrade. This is loud at compile time and does not corrupt data.

failure_scenarios.title: CLI and wizard login depend on a new auth 0.38 native-binding layout
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer installs or upgrades stash or @cipherstash/wizard and runs `stash auth login`, `stash init` or the wizard on a platform or package manager where the optional platform binary is not installed.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: auth 0.38 moved its platform bindings to optional peerDependencies (pnpm-lock). The CLI and wizard now list six platform packages as optionalDependencies through the catalog (pnpm-workspace.yaml:14-20). Platforms that are not listed, such as linux-arm64-musl and win32-arm64, have no binding. The auth API changes from 0.36 to 0.38 are unknown, and the wizard's test mocks @cipherstash/auth entirely.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The login and credential commands fail at module load on platforms where the binding is missing. The failure is loud and fixed by a patch release, but it blocks onboarding.
